```{=html}
  <div id="sd2-coefs"
       data-b0="`r if (knitr::is_html_output()) round(fixef(model_exch_apim)['Intercept','Estimate'], 2) else ''`"
       data-ba="`r if (knitr::is_html_output()) round(fixef(model_exch_apim)['communication_actor_gmc','Estimate'], 2) else ''`"
       data-bp="`r if (knitr::is_html_output()) round(fixef(model_exch_apim)['communication_partner_gmc','Estimate'], 2) else ''`"></div>

  <script>
  (function(){
    const root = document.currentScript.closest('section');
    const MIN = -5, MAX = 5, PLOT_DOMAIN = 5;
    const c = {actor:'#4E94F8', partner:'#A78BFA', cbc:'#E26A5C', cwc:'#FBBF24'};
    const coefData = root.querySelector('#sd2-coefs').dataset;
    const b0 = Number(coefData.b0), bA = Number(coefData.ba), bP = Number(coefData.bp);
    const bCbc = +(bA + bP).toFixed(2);
    const bCwc = +(bA - bP).toFixed(2);

    const el = id => root.querySelector('#' + id);
    const actor = el('sd2-actor'), partner = el('sd2-partner'), cbc = el('sd2-cbc'), cwc = el('sd2-cwc');
    const outA = el('sd2-out-actor'), outP = el('sd2-out-partner'), outCbc = el('sd2-out-cbc'), outCwc = el('sd2-out-cwc');
    const eqA = el('sd2-eq-apim'), eqD = el('sd2-eq-dim'), eqC = el('sd2-eq-coef');
    const point = el('sd2-point'), halo = el('sd2-halo'), svg = el('sd2-svg');

    const r1 = x => Math.round(Number(x) * 10) / 10;
    const fmt = x => (Math.abs(x) < 1e-10 ? 0 : x).toFixed(2);
    const mathNum = (x, color = null, result = false) => {
      const value = Math.abs(x) < 1e-10 ? 0 : x;
      const sign = value < 0 ? '−' : '<span class="sd2-sign-pad" aria-hidden="true"></span>';
      const style = color ? ` style="color:${color}"` : '';
      const cls = result ? 'sd2-result' : 'sd2-num';
      return `<span class="${cls}"${style}>${sign}${Math.abs(value).toFixed(2)}</span>`;
    };
    const beta = name => `<span class="sd2-beta">b<sub>${name}</sub></span>`;
    const xPix = x => 160 + x * (130 / PLOT_DOMAIN);
    const yPix = y => 160 - y * (130 / PLOT_DOMAIN);
    const clamp = (x, lo, hi) => Math.min(hi, Math.max(lo, Number(x)));

    function feasibleA(p){
      return [Math.max(MIN, 2 * MIN - p, 2 * MIN + p),
              Math.min(MAX, 2 * MAX - p, 2 * MAX + p)];
    }
    function feasibleP(a){
      return [Math.max(MIN, 2 * MIN - a, a - 2 * MAX),
              Math.min(MAX, 2 * MAX - a, a - 2 * MIN)];
    }
    function feasibleM(w){
      return [Math.max(MIN, MIN - w, MIN + w),
              Math.min(MAX, MAX - w, MAX + w)];
    }
    function feasibleW(m){
      return [Math.max(MIN, MIN - m, m - MAX),
              Math.min(MAX, MAX - m, m - MIN)];
    }

    function setFromAP(a, p){
      const aClamped = r1(clamp(a, MIN, MAX));
      const pClamped = r1(clamp(p, MIN, MAX));
      actor.value = aClamped;
      partner.value = pClamped;
      cbc.value = r1((aClamped + pClamped) / 2);
      cwc.value = r1((aClamped - pClamped) / 2);
      render();
    }
    function setFromDIM(m, w){
      const mClamped = r1(clamp(m, ...feasibleM(w)));
      const wClamped = r1(clamp(w, ...feasibleW(mClamped)));
      cbc.value = mClamped;
      cwc.value = wClamped;
      actor.value = r1(mClamped + wClamped);
      partner.value = r1(mClamped - wClamped);
      render();
    }
    function moveActor(){
      const p = r1(partner.value);
      const bounds = feasibleA(p);
      const a = r1(clamp(actor.value, bounds[0], bounds[1]));
      setFromAP(a, p);
    }
    function movePartner(){
      const a = r1(actor.value);
      const bounds = feasibleP(a);
      const p = r1(clamp(partner.value, bounds[0], bounds[1]));
      setFromAP(a, p);
    }
    function moveCbc(){
      const w = r1(cwc.value);
      const bounds = feasibleM(w);
      const m = r1(clamp(cbc.value, bounds[0], bounds[1]));
      setFromDIM(m, w);
    }
    function moveCwc(){
      const m = r1(cbc.value);
      const bounds = feasibleW(m);
      const w = r1(clamp(cwc.value, bounds[0], bounds[1]));
      setFromDIM(m, w);
    }

    function render(){
      const a = Number(actor.value), p = Number(partner.value), m = Number(cbc.value), w = Number(cwc.value);
      outA.value = a.toFixed(1); outP.value = p.toFixed(1); outCbc.value = m.toFixed(2); outCwc.value = w.toFixed(2);
      const yA = b0 + bA * a + bP * p;
      const yD = b0 + bCbc * m + bCwc * w;
      eqA.innerHTML = `<span class="sd2-var">Ŷ</span> = ${mathNum(b0)} + ${mathNum(bA)} <span class="sd2-times">×</span> ${mathNum(a, c.actor)} + ${mathNum(bP)} <span class="sd2-times">×</span> ${mathNum(p, c.partner)} = ${mathNum(yA, null, true)}`;
      eqD.innerHTML = `<span class="sd2-var">Ŷ</span> = ${mathNum(b0)} + ${mathNum(bCbc)} <span class="sd2-times">×</span> ${mathNum(m, c.cbc)} + ${mathNum(bCwc)} <span class="sd2-times">×</span> ${mathNum(w, c.cwc)} = ${mathNum(yD, null, true)}`;
      eqC.innerHTML = `${beta('cbc')} = ${mathNum(bA)} + ${mathNum(bP)} = ${mathNum(bCbc)}; &nbsp; ${beta('cwc')} = ${mathNum(bA)} − ${mathNum(bP)} = ${mathNum(bCwc)}`;
      point.setAttribute('cx', xPix(a)); point.setAttribute('cy', yPix(p));
      halo.setAttribute('cx', xPix(a)); halo.setAttribute('cy', yPix(p));
    }

    function drawGrid(){
      const g = el('sd2-grid-lines');
      const ticks = [-4, -2, 0, 2, 4];
      let html = '';
      ticks.forEach(t => {
        const main = t === 0 ? 1.5 : 1;
        html += `<line x1="${xPix(t)}" y1="30" x2="${xPix(t)}" y2="290" stroke="${c.actor}" stroke-opacity="${t===0?.48:.20}" stroke-width="${main}" stroke-dasharray="${t===0?'':'2 2'}"></line>`;
        html += `<line x1="30" y1="${yPix(t)}" x2="290" y2="${yPix(t)}" stroke="${c.partner}" stroke-opacity="${t===0?.48:.20}" stroke-width="${main}" stroke-dasharray="${t===0?'':'2 2'}"></line>`;
        html += `<line x1="${xPix(-PLOT_DOMAIN)}" y1="${yPix(2*t + PLOT_DOMAIN)}" x2="${xPix(PLOT_DOMAIN)}" y2="${yPix(2*t - PLOT_DOMAIN)}" stroke="${c.cbc}" stroke-opacity="${t===0?.50:.22}" stroke-width="${main}" stroke-dasharray="${t===0?'':'3 3'}"></line>`;
        html += `<line x1="${xPix(-PLOT_DOMAIN)}" y1="${yPix(-PLOT_DOMAIN - 2*t)}" x2="${xPix(PLOT_DOMAIN)}" y2="${yPix(PLOT_DOMAIN - 2*t)}" stroke="${c.cwc}" stroke-opacity="${t===0?.50:.22}" stroke-width="${main}" stroke-dasharray="${t===0?'':'3 3'}"></line>`;
      });
      g.innerHTML = html;
      el('sd2-axis-labels').innerHTML = `
        <text x="286" y="148" fill="${c.actor}" font-size="12" font-style="italic" font-weight="800" text-anchor="end">x<tspan baseline-shift="sub" font-size="8.5" font-style="normal">actor</tspan></text>
        <text x="150" y="22" fill="${c.partner}" font-size="12" font-style="italic" font-weight="800" text-anchor="middle">x<tspan baseline-shift="sub" font-size="8.5" font-style="normal">partner</tspan></text>
        <g transform="translate(${xPix(3.4)},${yPix(3.4)}) rotate(-45)"><text y="-7" fill="${c.cbc}" font-size="11" font-style="italic" font-weight="800" text-anchor="middle">x<tspan baseline-shift="sub" font-size="8" font-style="normal">cbc</tspan></text></g>
        <g transform="translate(${xPix(3.4)},${yPix(-3.4)}) rotate(45)"><text y="-7" fill="${c.cwc}" font-size="11" font-style="italic" font-weight="800" text-anchor="middle">x<tspan baseline-shift="sub" font-size="8" font-style="normal">cwc</tspan></text></g>`;
    }

    function gridToAP(evt){
      const rect = svg.getBoundingClientRect();
      const clientX = evt.touches ? evt.touches[0].clientX : evt.clientX;
      const clientY = evt.touches ? evt.touches[0].clientY : evt.clientY;
      const sx = ((clientX - rect.left) / rect.width) * 320;
      const sy = ((clientY - rect.top) / rect.height) * 320;
      setFromAP(r1((sx - 160) / (130 / PLOT_DOMAIN)), r1((160 - sy) / (130 / PLOT_DOMAIN)));
    }
    let dragging = false;
    svg.addEventListener('mousedown', evt => { dragging = true; gridToAP(evt); });
    svg.addEventListener('mousemove', evt => { if (dragging) gridToAP(evt); });
    window.addEventListener('mouseup', () => { dragging = false; });
    svg.addEventListener('touchstart', evt => { dragging = true; gridToAP(evt); }, {passive:true});
    svg.addEventListener('touchmove', evt => { if (dragging) gridToAP(evt); }, {passive:true});
    window.addEventListener('touchend', () => { dragging = false; });

    actor.addEventListener('input', moveActor);
    partner.addEventListener('input', movePartner);
    cbc.addEventListener('input', moveCbc);
    cwc.addEventListener('input', moveCwc);
    function bindButton(id, fn){
      const button = el(id);
      button.addEventListener('pointerdown', evt => evt.stopPropagation());
      button.addEventListener('click', evt => {
        evt.preventDefault();
        evt.stopPropagation();
        fn();
      });
    }
    bindButton('sd2-reset', () => setFromAP(0, 0));
    bindButton('sd2-demo-mean', () => setFromAP(1, 1));
    bindButton('sd2-demo-deviation', () => setFromAP(1, -1));

    drawGrid();
    setFromAP(0, 0);
  })();
  </script>
```

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}

In the interactive HTML slides, this section contains sliders that demonstrate
the APIM–DIM reparameterization. In this static version:

* actor and partner predictors are rewritten as a dyad-level mean and a
  within-dyad half-difference; and
* the DIM coefficients are a linear reparameterization of the APIM coefficients,
  so fitted values are unchanged.

```text
x_cbc = (x_actor_gmc + x_partner_gmc) / 2
x_cwc = (x_actor_gmc - x_partner_gmc) / 2
```

:::


## Equivalence APIM and DIM

* If the couple mean goes up by 1 and the within-couple deviation from the couple
mean stays fixed, this means that both partners' predictors must go up by 1 unit.
Thus, the effects are linear combinations:

$$b_{cbc} = b_{actor\_gmc} + b_{partner\_gmc}$$

* Similarly, if a person's deviation from their couple mean is one unit higher and
the couple mean stays fixed, this means their partners' deviation must be one unit lower.
Thus, the effects are a linear combination:

$$b_{cwc} = b_{actor\_gmc} - b_{partner\_gmc}$$

[@Bolger2025Unified]

## Equivalence APIM and DIM

* Conversely, to obtain the actor and partner effects given the DIM estimates:

$$b_{actor\_gmc} = \frac{b_{cbc} + b_{cwc}}{2}$$

$$b_{partner\_gmc} = \frac{b_{cbc} - b_{cwc}}{2}$$

## Equivalence APIM and DIM

Example: using APIM coefficients to obtain DIM coefficients and computing *Credible Intervals* of DIM coefficients.

```{r compare-exch-apim-dim-hypothesis, cache=TRUE, dependson='fit-exch-apim-brms'}
a <- hypothesis(
  model_exch_apim,
  "communication_actor_gmc + communication_partner_gmc = 0"
)

round(a$hypothesis[,c(2,3,4,5)], 2)
```

:::column

## Equivalence APIM and DIM: Takeaway

* **APIM** and **DIM** are reparametrizations of the same model
* **APIM**: intuitive actor/partner framing
* **DIM**: clean separation of between vs within components
* Estimating one model allows for directly obtaining estimates of the other
* Same random-effects structure at dyad level and same assumptions

### Side Note:

In the **distinguishable** case, the **Dyadic Score Model (DSM)** [e.g., @stadlerHowCompanionshipRelated2023] is equivalent to the APIM! [@Bolger2025Unified; @iidaModelsInterdependentIndividuals2018]



## Exchangeable Dyads - L-DIM/L-APIM: Simulated Data

We use the same data as in the exchangeable case. But we don't need the gender-related variables anymore, as we assume
that partners are indistinguishable.

```{r data-exch-long-apim-source, echo=FALSE, results='hide', cache=TRUE, dependson='data-dist-long-apim-center'}

required_long_apim_cols <- c(
  'userID', 'coupleID', 'couple_day', 'diaryday', 'diaryday_c',
  'member', 'closeness',
  'provided_support_actor', 'provided_support_partner',
  'provided_support_actor_cbp', 'provided_support_actor_cwp',
  'provided_support_partner_cbp', 'provided_support_partner_cwp'
)

if (!all(required_long_apim_cols %in% names(df_long_apim))) {
  df_long_apim <- bmlm::isolate(
    df_long_apim,
    by = 'userID',
    value = c('provided_support_actor', 'provided_support_partner'),
    which = 'both'
  ) %>%
    rename(
      provided_support_actor_cwp = provided_support_actor_cw,
      provided_support_partner_cwp = provided_support_partner_cw,
      provided_support_actor_cbp = provided_support_actor_cb,
      provided_support_partner_cbp = provided_support_partner_cb
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      member = ifelse(gender == 1, 1, 2),
      couple_day = interaction(coupleID, diaryday, drop = TRUE),
      diaryday_c = scale(diaryday, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
    )
}

df_long_apim2 <- df_long_apim %>%
  dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(required_long_apim_cols))

```

# Exchangeable Dyads - Intensive Longitudinal

## Exchangeable Dyads - Longitudinal DIM/APIM

* We need an APIM or DIM on both the between person level and the within-person level.
* Due to equivalence, we could have a DIM on one level and an APIM on the other.

If we want a within-person DIM:

```{r data-exch-long-dim-create, cache=TRUE, dependson='data-exch-long-apim-source'}
df_long_dim <- df_long_apim2 %>%
  mutate(

    # Between Person Level DIM (centering between couples and within couple between person)
    provided_support_cbc = (provided_support_actor_cbp + provided_support_partner_cbp) / 2,
    provided_support_cwcbp = (provided_support_actor_cbp - provided_support_partner_cbp) / 2,

    # Within Person Level DIM (couple mean and deviation on each day)
    provided_support_cwp_mean = (provided_support_actor_cwp + provided_support_partner_cwp) / 2,
    provided_support_cwp_halfdiff = (provided_support_actor_cwp - provided_support_partner_cwp) / 2
  )


```

## Exchangeable Dyads - L-DIM/L-APIM: Preparing the Mean-Deviation Idiff Approach

We need to randomly assign -1 and +1 for each Partner within each couple.
This will be needed for contrast coding the intercept.

For example:

```{r example-exch-long-idiff, eval = FALSE}

df_long_dim <- df_long_dim %>%
  group_by(coupleID) %>%
  mutate(
    base = ifelse(userID == min(userID), 1, -1),
    flip = 1 - 2 * rbinom(1, 1, 0.5),   # yields +1 or -1 once per couple
    Idiff = base * flip,

    # Not needed for brms, but for glmmTMB we create two dummy variables representing
    # randomly selected partner 1 and partner 2.
    is_partner1 = as.numeric(Idiff == 1),
    is_partner2 = as.numeric(Idiff == -1)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  relocate(Idiff, .after = coupleID) %>%
  relocate(is_partner1, is_partner2, .after = Idiff) %>%
  dplyr::select(-base, -flip)


print_df(print_couple_preview(df_long_dim, couple_id = "31"))

```

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}

```{r data-exch-long-dim-preview, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, dependson='data-exch-long-dim-create', eval=knitr::is_latex_output()}

  print_couple_preview_for_output(
    df_long_dim,
    couple_id = "31",
    pdf_cols = c(
      "userID", "coupleID", "diaryday", "diaryday_c", "member",
      "provided_support_cbc", "provided_support_cwcbp",
      "provided_support_cwp_mean", "provided_support_cwp_halfdiff"
    )
  ),
  font_size = 6
)
```

## Exchangeable Dyads - L-DIM/L-APIM: Preparing the Mean-Deviation Idiff Approach

```{r data-exch-long-idiff, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, dependson='data-exch-long-dim-create'}
set.seed(123)
df_long_dim <- df_long_dim %>%
  group_by(coupleID) %>%
  mutate(
    base = ifelse(userID == min(userID), 1, -1),
    flip = 1 - 2 * rbinom(1, 1, 0.5),   # yields +1 or -1 once per couple
    Idiff = base * flip,
    is_partner1 = as.numeric(Idiff == 1),
    is_partner2 = as.numeric(Idiff == -1)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  relocate(Idiff, .after = coupleID) %>%
  relocate(is_partner1, is_partner2, .after = Idiff) %>%
  dplyr::select(-base, -flip)


print_df(
  print_couple_preview_for_output(
    df_long_dim,
    couple_id = "31",
    days = 0:4,
    pdf_cols = c(
      "userID", "coupleID", "Idiff", "is_partner1", "is_partner2",
      "diaryday", "diaryday_c", "provided_support_cbc",
      "provided_support_cwcbp", "provided_support_cwp_mean",
      "provided_support_cwp_halfdiff"
    )
  ),
  font_size = if (knitr::is_latex_output()) 6 else 20
)

```


## Exchangeable Dyads - L-DIM/L-APIM: glmmTMB

```{r fit-exch-long-apim-glmmtmb, eval=FALSE, results='hide', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#| code-line-numbers: "1-4|6-11|13-18|20-21|23-28|30-34|36-39"

model_exch_long_apim_glmmtmb <- glmmTMB(
  closeness ~ 1 +

    diaryday_c +

    # Within-person APIM
    provided_support_actor_cwp +
    provided_support_partner_cwp +
    # Equivalent to within-person DIM:
    # provided_support_cwp_mean +
    # provided_support_cwp_halfdiff +

    # Between-person APIM
    provided_support_actor_cbp +
    provided_support_partner_cbp +
    # Equivalent to between-person DIM
    # provided_support_cwcbp+
    # provided_support_cbc +

    # Dyad-Level intercept and slopes for time-varying predictors
    (1 + diaryday_c + provided_support_actor_cwp + provided_support_partner_cwp | coupleID) +

    # Both partners' deviations from these dyad-level means and slopes.
    # Note: separate random-effects block to make them uncorrelated with dyad-level REs.
    (0 + Idiff +
         I(Idiff * diaryday_c) +
         I(Idiff * provided_support_actor_cwp) +
         I(Idiff * provided_support_partner_cwp) | coupleID) +

    # After accounting for stable differences between partners, they may still be
    # non-independent each day due to external occurrences and daily exchange processes
    # not captured in the fixed effects. Thus, residuals are not yet independent.
    # Homogeneous same-day residual covariance between partners:
    homcs(0 + is_partner1 + is_partner2 | coupleID:diaryday)

  # We remove the additional independent residual variance
  # (only if the family has a native residual!)
  , dispformula = ~ 0
  , data = df_long_dim
)
```

## Exchangeable Dyads - L-DIM/L-APIM: glmmTMB

```{r results-exch-long-apim-glmmtmb, eval=FALSE, echo=FALSE, class.output='model-summary-output'}
summary(model_exch_long_apim_glmmtmb)
```

In this example, the glmmTMB model does not converge properly. The random-effects structure is too complex for the information available in these data, so we would have to simplify it. Instead, we use brms below.

## Exchangeable Dyads - L-DIM/L-APIM: brms

In brms, the same model can be estimated as:

::: {.brms-prior-note}
Unlike the distinguishable longitudinal model, this exchangeable specification keeps one pooled residual `sigma` (`sigma ~ 1` is implied). Its residual SD prior therefore targets `class = "sigma"` directly.
:::

```{r fit-exch-long-apim-brms, results='hide', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, cache=TRUE, dependson='data-exch-long-idiff'}
#| code-line-numbers: "1-4|6-12|14-15|17-22|24-25|27-29"

formula_exch_long_apim <- bf(
  closeness ~ 1 +

    diaryday_c +

    # Within-person APIM
    provided_support_actor_cwp +
    provided_support_partner_cwp +

    # Between-person APIM
    provided_support_actor_cbp +
    provided_support_partner_cbp +

    # Dyad-Level intercept and slopes for time-varying predictors
    (1 + diaryday_c + provided_support_actor_cwp + provided_support_partner_cwp | coupleID) +

    # Both partners' deviations from these dyad-level means and slopes.
    # Note: separate random-effects block to make them uncorrelated with dyad-level REs.
    (0 + Idiff +
         I(Idiff * diaryday_c) +
         I(Idiff * provided_support_actor_cwp) +
         I(Idiff * provided_support_partner_cwp) | coupleID) +

    # Modelling Level 1 residuals in brms:
    unstr(time = member, gr = couple_day)

  # Again, no need to model heterogeneous residual variances (sigma)
  # Implied: sigma = ~ 1
)

priors_exch_long_apim <- c(
  prior(normal(4, 2), class = "Intercept"),
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b"),
  prior(exponential(1), class = "sd"),
  prior(lkj(2), class = "cor"),
  prior(student_t(3, 0, 1.5), class = "sigma"),
  prior(lkj(2), class = "cortime")
)

model_exch_long_apim <- brm(
  formula = formula_exch_long_apim,
  data = df_long_dim,
  family = gaussian(link = identity),
  prior = priors_exch_long_apim,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  iter = 2000,
  warmup = 1000,
  seed = 123,
  file = file.path('brms_cache', 'model_apim_ind_long_apim')
)


```

## Exchangeable Dyads - L-DIM/L-APIM: brms

The equivalent DIM specification:

```{r fit-exch-long-dim-brms, results='hide', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, cache=TRUE, dependson='data-exch-long-idiff'}
#| code-line-numbers: "7-11|13-17| 19-20"

# DIM Version
formula_exch_long_dim <- bf(
  closeness ~ 1 +

    diaryday_c +

    provided_support_cwp_mean +
    provided_support_cwp_halfdiff +

    provided_support_cbc +
    provided_support_cwcbp +

    (1 + diaryday_c + provided_support_actor_cwp + provided_support_partner_cwp | coupleID) +
    (0 + Idiff +
         I(Idiff * diaryday_c) +
         I(Idiff * provided_support_actor_cwp) +
         I(Idiff * provided_support_partner_cwp) | coupleID) +

    unstr(time = member, gr = couple_day)
)

priors_exch_long_dim <- c(
  prior(normal(4, 2), class = "Intercept"),
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b"),
  prior(exponential(1), class = "sd"),
  prior(lkj(2), class = "cor"),
  prior(student_t(3, 0, 1.5), class = "sigma"),
  prior(lkj(2), class = "cortime")
)

model_exch_long_dim <- brm(
  formula = formula_exch_long_dim,
  data = df_long_dim,
  family = gaussian(link = identity),
  prior = priors_exch_long_dim,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  iter = 2000,
  warmup = 1000,
  seed = 123,
  file = file.path('brms_cache', 'model_apim_ind_long_dim')
)


```


## Exchangeable Dyads - L-DIM/L-APIM: Explanation Idiff

For appropriate exchangeable random effects, we can use mean-deviation `Idiff` coding [@delrosarioPracticalGuideSpecifying2025; @kenny_ackerman_2023]:

* Randomly give one partner a constant of -1 and the other a constant of 1
* The couple-level intercept represents the average/common intercept of the two partners. `(1 | coupleID)`
* A column of 1s and -1s represents each partner's deviation from the couple-level effect, with partners contributing equally in opposite directions (+1 and -1)

Exchangeability is retained: if partners are flipped, the result is the same.

(@delrosarioPracticalGuideSpecifying2025 provide practical guidance on how to reduce the random effects structure in case of non-convergence.)

## Exchangeable Dyads - L-DIM/L-APIM: `homcs` and Idiff

For two partners coded with `Idiff = +1` and `Idiff = -1`, the glmmTMB residual structures `homcs(0 + is_partner1 + is_partner2 | coupleID:diaryday)` and `(1 | coupleID:diaryday) + (0 + Idiff | coupleID:diaryday)` imply the same homogeneous two-partner residual covariance.

This equivalence assumes exactly two rows per couple-day, independent common/couple-mean and `Idiff` deviation random-effect blocks, and `dispformula = ~ 0`.

The model code keeps `homcs(...)` because it states the residual structure more directly.

It also does not need back-transformation.

## Extract Full APIM Random Effects Variance-Covariance Matrix

We can rotate the random effects structure back to obtain the full APIM Random effects variance-covariance matrix, based on
[@kenny_ackerman_2023].
Just as we would in a SEM model with equality constraints!

For example, the within-partner variance of the random intercept is:

$$
\operatorname{Var}(u_{\text{common intercept}}) +
\operatorname{Var}(u_{\text{Idiff intercept}})
$$

and the cross-partner covariance of both partners' random intercepts is:

$$
\operatorname{Var}(u_{\text{common intercept}}) -
\operatorname{Var}(u_{\text{Idiff intercept}})
$$

In the model output, the common-intercept variance is labelled `Intercept`, and the deviation-intercept variance is labelled `Idiff`.
This rotation only holds when the common/couple-mean and `Idiff` deviation random effects are uncorrelated. This is why we put them in separate random-effects blocks.

## Extract Full APIM Random Effects Variance-Covariance Matrix

```{r extract-exch-long-apim-covariance, cache=TRUE, dependson='fit-exch-long-apim-brms'}
a <- summarize_exchangeable_apim_brms(
  model_exch_long_apim,
  gr = "coupleID",
  idiff = "Idiff",
  partner_labels = c("PartnerA", "PartnerB")
)

```

## Extract Full APIM Random Effects Variance-Covariance Matrix: Within-Person Matrix

```{r results-exch-long-apim-cov-within}
print_df(a$within_person_covariance_matrix)
```


## Extract Full APIM Random Effects Variance-Covariance Matrix: Cross-Person Matrix

```{r results-exch-long-apim-cov-cross}

```


## Extract Full APIM Random Effects Variance-Covariance Matrix: Full Matrix

```{r results-exch-long-apim-cov-full}
print_wide_matrix(a$full_covariance_matrix, font_size = 6)
```


The helper function `summarize_exchangeable_apim_brms()` is defined in `00_R_Functions/ReportModels.R`. It rotates every posterior draw, so the interval estimates for the transformed SDs, correlations, covariances, and residual quantities are computed on the transformed scale.

For `glmmTMB`, the same back-transformation is algebraically possible, but interval estimation is less direct because there are no posterior draws. One would usually transform parametric bootstrap draws or asymptotic draws from the fitted parameter covariance matrix.
